newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks power ahead at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks power ahead at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks surged at the close on Monday on heavy bidding by international investors, dealers said.

"The market boosted the rally it began Friday after clearing options expirations, and it was powered by a wave of foreign buying, which will probably carry on Tuesday," said dealer Emilio Alessandro of brokers Alessandro.
The blue-chip MerVal index jumped 2.5 percent in hefty turnover to close at 759.17. On Friday it rose 1.8 percent, taking the week's gains to 2.1 percent.
Floor volume swelled to 41.7 million pesos from 36.4 million Friday, while over-the-counter deals picked up to 116.2 million pesos from 93 million Friday.
"Today's huge turnover shows the market is going through a very good patch, but it could also cause some volatility if it grows too much too soon," said Alessandro.
Analysts welcomed industrial output data by consultants FIEL which showed a 5.1 percent rise for 1996. "It wasn't a surprise but it fed the bullish mood," one trader said.
He noted market bellwether YPF, Argentina's oil giant, shot up 2.9 percent despite a slide in crude oil prices.
The broad market index closed up 2.1 percent, with winners beating losers 62 to five and 78 issues closing flat.
Top main-tier performers were steelmaker Acindar, holding company Comercial del Plata and Banco de Galicia, which rocketed 6.2 percent, 5.6 percent and 4.3 percent, respectively.
The only MerVal losers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, construction stock Polledo and real estate developer Irsa, off 1.3 percent, 0.9 percent and 0.3 percent, respectively.
